domain_restrictions: A,B,d are integers with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0
Empty product convention: if d=0 then ∏_{i=1}^0 (...) = 1 so Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1
Assumption: the rational expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) is actually a polynomial, i.e., Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q] (not just a rational function)
Graded ring S is Q[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_i)=B+i for i=1..d
If d=0, interpret S as Q (no variables, hence no f_i witnesses needed)
Each f_i is homogeneous in S with weighted degree deg(f_i)=A+i
Regularity condition: in the successive quotient S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}), the class of f_i is not a zero-divisor (equivalently: (f_1,...,f_d) is a homogeneous regular sequence in S)
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Let A,B,d ∈ Z with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, and define Q_{A,B,d}(q)=∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) with Q_{A,B,0}(q)=1. If Q_{A,B,d}(q) ∈ Q[q], then in the weighted graded polynomial ring S=Q[x_1,...,x_d] (or S=Q if d=0) with deg(x_i)=B+i, there exist homogeneous elements f_1,...,f_d ∈ S such that deg(f_i)=A+i for each i=1..d and for each i the class of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor (so f_1,...,f_d form a homogeneous regular sequence). Consequently, the graded data of S modulo this regular sequence yields the given expression Q_{A,B,d}(q) (as stated in the equivalence).

Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) := ∏_{i=1}^d (1-q^{A+i})/(1-q^{B+i}) belongs to Q[q] (q formal indeterminate)
There exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that for each i=1..d: deg(f_i)=A+i, and the image of f_i in S/(f_1,...,f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: For integers A, B, d with A >= B >= 0 and d >= 0, define Q_{A,B,d}(q) := prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(A+i)) / (1 - q^(B+i)), with the empty product equal to 1 when d = 0. Assume Q_{A,B,d}(q) belongs to Q[q]. Let S be the weighted polynomial ring Q[x_1, ..., x_d] graded by deg(x_i) = B+i; when d = 0 interpret S as Q. Then there exist homogeneous polynomials f_1, ..., f_d in S such that deg(f_i) = A+i for every i, and for each i the image of f_i in S/(f_1, ..., f_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor. Equivalently, Q_{A,B,d}(q) is realized by a homogeneous regular sequence in a weighted polynomial ring with variable weights B+1, ..., B+d and relation degrees A+1, ..., A+d.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Let M_i = S/(g_1,...,g_i) for 0 <= i <= d, with M_0 = S. Since each g_i is homogeneous, each ideal (g_1,...,g_i) is homogeneous, so each M_i inherits a grading. Because all weights w_j are positive, the degree-n piece S_n is finite-dimensional over k: it has basis the monomials x_1^{a_1}...x_d^{a_d} with a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d = n, and there are only finitely many such tuples. Hence every (M_i)_n is finite-dimensional as a quotient of S_n, so all Hilbert series below are well-defined.

First compute Hilb_S(q). The monomials form a k-basis of S, and deg(x_1^{a_1}...x_d^{a_d}) = a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d. Therefore, as a formal power series,
Hilb_S(q) = sum_{a_1,...,a_d >= 0} q^{a_1 w_1 + ... + a_d w_d} = prod_{j=1}^d (sum_{m >= 0} q^{m w_j}) = 1 / prod_{j=1}^d (1 - q^{w_j}).
When d = 0, this is the empty product 1, which equals Hilb_k(q).

Now fix i with 1 <= i <= d, and let g_i_bar be the image of g_i in M_{i-1}. Because g_1,...,g_d is a regular sequence, g_i_bar is a non-zero-divisor on M_{i-1}. Let e_i = deg(g_i). Consider the shifted graded module M_{i-1}(-e_i), defined by M_{i-1}(-e_i)_n = (M_{i-1})_{n-e_i}. Multiplication by g_i_bar gives a degree-preserving map
M_{i-1}(-e_i) -> M_{i-1},   m |-> g_i_bar m.
It is injective because g_i_bar is a non-zero-divisor, and its cokernel is M_{i-1}/g_i_bar M_{i-1}, which is naturally isomorphic to S/(g_1,...,g_i) = M_i. Thus we have a short exact sequence of graded k-vector spaces
0 -> M_{i-1}(-e_i) -> M_{i-1} -> M_i -> 0.

Taking degree-n parts and dimensions, for every n we get
dim_k((M_i)_n) = dim_k((M_{i-1})_n) - dim_k((M_{i-1})_{n-e_i}),
where the last term is understood as 0 if n - e_i < 0. Summing over n >= 0 shows
Hilb_{M_i}(q) = Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q) - q^{e_i} Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q) = (1 - q^{e_i}) Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q),
because by definition of the shift, Hilb_{M_{i-1}(-e_i)}(q) = q^{e_i} Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q).

Iterating this identity for i = 1,2,...,d yields
Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = Hilb_{M_d}(q) = Hilb_S(q) prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i}) = (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{e_i})) / (prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^{w_i})).
This is exactly the claimed formula.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Given a weighted graded polynomial ring S equal to k[x_1,...,x_d] with deg(x_i)=w_i where k is a field, d is a nonnegative integer, and each w_i is a positive integer, suppose g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S such that deg(g_i)=e_i for each i. Then the graded Hilbert series of the quotient ring S modulo the ideal generated by g_1,...,g_d is equal to the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the e_i) divided by the product over i from 1 to d of (1 minus q to the w_i).

payload.statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] be graded by deg(x_i)=w_i. If g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence in S and deg(g_i)=e_i for each i, then the graded Hilbert series of the quotient is Hilb_{S/(g_1,...,g_d)}(q) = prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(e_i)) / prod_{i=1}^d (1 - q^(w_i)).

detailed_findings.finding: The proof correctly justifies that each graded piece is finite-dimensional because all weights are positive, so the Hilbert series manipulations are legitimate as formal power series.

result_payload.reason: The proof gives the standard complete Hilbert-series argument for a homogeneous regular sequence in a positively weighted polynomial ring. It verifies finite-dimensionality of graded pieces, computes Hilb_S(q)=1/\prod_i(1-q^{w_i}), constructs for each i the exact sequence 0 -> M_{i-1}(-e_i) -> M_{i-1} -> M_i -> 0 using the non-zero-divisor property of g_i, deduces Hilb_{M_i}(q)=(1-q^{e_i})Hilb_{M_{i-1}}(q), and iterates to obtain the claimed formula. The proof matches the lemma sketch and role in the assembly, with no semantic drift or dependency issues.
